name: Vikran Engineering Ltd
title: Vikran Engineering Ltd - 544496 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vikran Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.2% YoY to INR204 crore and PAT 209.9% to INR17.5 crore, while consolidated PAT was only INR4 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.5% in Q1 FY26 (>500 bps improvement)
Management also cited INR64 crores in one answer

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Largest part of order book at 62%; about INR70 crores of Q1 revenue from solar projects other than NOPL, plus INR62 crores from NOPL. The 969 MW NOPL project (INR3,518 crores incl. GST) is under direct EPC order from NOPL.

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: 28% of order book. Q1 revenue came mainly from EHV and PD projects (balance after solar and water, not separately quantified). Recent wins: INR530 crores from MSEDCL (April) and INR120 crores from Power Grid (400 kV GIS substation package).

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: About 10% of order book; about INR12 crores of Q1 revenue. Carries a provision of about INR6.5 crores due to slow Jal Jeevan Mission receivables recovery; about INR120 crores of debtors are tied to JJM projects.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from NOPL in standalone INR204 crores and why growth only 28%?
qa_highlights.answer: NOPL contributed about INR62 crores; management attributed low H1 to seasonality and client budget constraints, with H2 expected to be heavy against INR2,200-2,500 crores FY27 execution target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited higher project costs, about INR6.5 crores provision on Jal Jeevan receivables (reversible on collection), and NOPL overheads booked without revenue at consolidated level; standalone margins described as normal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated revenue lower than standalone and which to track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NOPL work is capitalised as asset in consolidation since it is now a 100% subsidiary; standalone revenue to be used until NOPL plant is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Jal Jeevan Mission receivables and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital in JJM projects fixed at a set level; about INR120 crores of JJM debtors; about INR23 crores received last quarter and more than INR10 crores in the last 30 days, with central funds of about INR17,000 crores released to UP.

qa_highlights.question: Status of NOPL debt financing (INR3,100 crores) from IREDA and other lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Final IREDA committee sanction expected this quarter, with disbursement expected in the same window; financial closure targeted in Q1 per management, with 75:25 debt-equity cited.

qa_highlights.question: Status of INR29 crore disputed receivable in court?
qa_highlights.answer: Only INR29 crores certified by client is booked; claim is much higher; no timeline given as matter is in court, but management is hopeful of positive outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Debtor days at 296 — has it peaked?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said this is the peak and debtor days should improve by end FY27, with some improvement visible in H1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone execution target of INR2,200-2,500 crores against order book of about INR6,496 crores; H2 expected to be heavy.
NOPL revenue plan of about INR1,500 crores in FY27 (about INR100 crores in September, remaining about INR1,400 crores in H2); described as conservative, with possible quarter-to-quarter slippage.
EBITDA margin guided to remain in the 14%-17% range blended, consistent with last four years, per CFO.
Management expects to be cash positive by end of FY27 if 650 MW of NOPL solar is commissioned.
NOPL project completion expected within 12 months; management says it is on track; debtor days expected to improve by end FY27.
Consolidated financials expected to become meaningful after NOPL plant commissioning, with over INR500 crores revenue and 80%-89% EBITDA cited for the power-generation phase from next year.
capex_capacity: NOPL 969 MW AC solar project in Maharashtra: about 45 MW commissioned across nine sites, 15 MW ready to commission in coming days, and advanced stages for about 240 MW; about 265 MW out of 969 MW cited as in advanced execution.

Project cost cited at about INR4,000 crores (debt portion about INR3,100 crores); funding split of about 75:25 debt-equity; IREDA sanction previously given, final committee sanction and disbursement expected within Q2.
CFA subsidy of about INR1,017 crores cited as backup refinancing source.
Commissioned 132 kV Miao-Namsai transmission line in Arunachal Pradesh (40.6 km, 138 towers); second such line in six months.
Management says solar and Power T&D are asset-carved into SPV, with 25-year PPA with MSEDCL for NOPL power.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR6,496 crores: solar EPC 62%, Power T&D 28%, water about 10%.
Q1 orders: about INR530 crores from MSEDCL (distribution, Nashik and Kolhapur, ADB-funded) and about INR120 crores from Power Grid (400 kV GIS substation extension).
Management cited company's bidding stance: avoiding aggressive bids at 8%-9% EBITDA margin, targeting higher-margin orders.
Data centre: no order yet; quotes made; target of at least one order by end FY27 with consultant E&Y.
Overseas: Middle East projects delayed; West Asia conflict price variation passed through to clients; focus remains domestic.
risks_watch: Execution concentration: NOPL 969 MW project carries about 62% solar EPC weight in order book; needs about INR1,400 crores of revenue in H2 to meet plan.
Working capital and funding: NOPL equity (about 25%) and any shortfall to be met from internal accruals; management cited backup options but no committed sign-off yet.
Receivables: Jal Jeevan Mission dues (about INR120 crores debtors) and INR29 crore disputed receivable pending in court; debtor days at 296.
Consolidated profitability gap: consolidated PAT INR4 crores vs standalone INR17.5 crores; consolidated EBITDA margin about 8%.
Watch next quarter: NOPL financial closure and disbursement, Q2 NOPL revenue of about INR100 crores, debtor-day trend, and first data-centre order.
Geopolitical: West Asia conflict cited as delaying Middle East opportunities.
key_quotes: So, we are pretty confident because it is, so the way we look at it is not a single massive project of 969 megawatt.
So, kindly have some patience till for the end of this financial year, as I committed by end of this financial year, we will be the cash positive.
So, this is a very positive movement and in the recovery of our receivables what we kept the target for the Q1, Q2, Q4, and we have, we are meeting and we are going exactly as per the schedule.
And this is, we are bullish on going for a developer mode project.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, standalone profit growth and NOPL timelines, but defensive on the standalone-versus-consolidated revenue gap and repeatedly deflecting detailed margin and cost questions to standalone figures. Management was vague on the data-centre revenue potential and gave no timeline for the court case.
